action: Roll back the last BGP config change on the edge router, then clear the BGP session and verify prefix counts return to baseline.
root_cause: Faulty or untested BGP policy/config change caused session instability.
symptom: BGP neighbor flap after a config change on an edge router

action: Clean and reseat the optic; if errors persist, replace the optic and re-test the link.
root_cause: Degraded optic on the BGP peering link.
symptom: BGP neighbor flap with interface errors on the same link

action: Shift traffic to the alternate uplink via BGP local-preference, and apply QoS policing to bulk traffic classes.
root_cause: Traffic failed over onto a single uplink after a neighbor/link loss.
symptom: Uplink saturation after a traffic shift or failover

action: Reroute affected prefixes over the alternate path and confirm loss returns below 1% before closing.
root_cause: Congestion on the saturated uplink drops packets under load.
symptom: Packet loss on downstream links following uplink saturation

action: Clean connectors, reseat the optic, and replace it if Rx power stays below -24 dBm.
root_cause: Dirty or failing optic / bent fiber on the core link.
symptom: Optical Rx power steadily degrading on a core link

action: Merge duplicate tickets into the primary incident ticket and keep a single timeline for customer updates.
root_cause: Alert fatigue: several monitoring tools and engineers opened tickets for one incident.
symptom: Multiple tickets opened for the same outage by different tools and engineers

action: Apply control-plane policing and rate-limit non-essential management traffic, then monitor CPU for 15 minutes.
root_cause: Control-plane overload starving the BGP process.
symptom: BGP drops correlated with high CPU on the edge router

action: Set both ends to auto-negotiation (or matching fixed speed/duplex) and clear interface counters.
root_cause: Speed/duplex mismatch after a manual interface change.
symptom: Interface errors and flapping after a speed/duplex change

action: Apply remotely-triggered blackholing (RTBH) for the target prefix or divert traffic to scrubbing.
root_cause: Volumetric traffic flood (likely DDoS) toward one destination.
symptom: Sudden uplink saturation from a single source prefix

action: Reseat the line card, verify power feeds and airflow, and replace the faulty PSU if alarms repeat.
root_cause: Power supply or cooling failure resetting a line card.
symptom: Line-card reset after a power or cooling alarm
